step_by_step_reasoning:
The architecture diagram and transcript describe Hexagon Digital Reality's geospatial data processing platform across two AWS accounts/environments (AWS Data on the left, AWS User/Pro on the right).

1. Visual & Audio Inventory:
- User (Top Center): Representing end users, architects, and field devices uploading geospatial data.
- AWS Data Account (Left):
  - S3 Data: Centralized storage bucket holding primary geospatial data.
  - EKS Data: Managed Kubernetes cluster handling streaming and data logic.
- VPC Peering (Center): Enables cross-account, private communication between AWS Data and User/Pro environments.
- AWS User/Pro Account (Right):
  - EKS User/Pro: Managed Kubernetes cluster running containerized microservices that listen to queues and manage UI/processing workflows.
  - SQS: Queue storing S3 event notifications and decoupled processing task messages.
  - ASG (Auto Scaling Group): EC2 instances configured with templates pulling container images from ECR to execute pipeline processing stages.
  - S3 User/Pro: Bucket where users directly upload raw data via pre-signed URLs and receive processed outputs.

2. Flows & Sequence:
- Flow 0 (Cross-Account Data Streaming): S3 Data -> EKS Data -> VPC Peering -> EKS User/Pro.
- Flow 1 (Upload & Async Processing Pipeline):
  - User uploads file directly to S3 User/Pro.
  - S3 User/Pro triggers event message to SQS queue.
  - EKS User/Pro container listens to SQS.
  - Task info is dispatched from SQS to Auto Scaling Group (EC2 instances).
  - ASG processing workers save final output back to S3 User/Pro.

edges.notes: EKS Data accesses raw geospatial data stored in S3 Data bucket.
EKS Data routes data streams across account boundaries via VPC Peering.
VPC Peering securely delivers data to EKS User/Pro across the AWS backbone network.
User uploads file directly to S3 User/Pro bucket using a pre-signed URL.
S3 event notification triggers an upload event message into SQS.
Container on EKS User/Pro listens to and polls SQS for incoming messages.
SQS messaging system dispatches task information to EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling Group.
Processed geospatial output files are written back from EC2 instances to S3 User/Pro.
